es.summary: La furosemida es un diurético de asa usado para eliminar exceso de líquido en insuficiencia cardíaca y edema.
key_points: Bloquea Na⁺/Cl⁻ en el asa de Henle, aumentando la diuresis.
Puede causar hipopotasemia, hiponatremia y ototoxicidad.
Monitorizar presión arterial, electrolitos y función renal antes y durante el tratamiento.
Evitar su uso con NSAIDs que reducen su eficacia.

mechanism: Inhibe la reabsorción de sodio, cloro y potasio en el asa de Henle.
Reduce el gradiente osmótico, aumentando la excreción de agua.
Produce una diuresis potente y rápida.
indications: Insuficiencia cardíaca con sobrecarga de volumen.
Edema pulmonar o periférico por enfermedad renal o hepática.
Hipertensión resistente cuando se combina con otros antihipertensivos.
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad a la furosemida o a otros sulfonamidas.
Anuria o insuficiencia renal aguda sin diuresis.
interactions: Inhibidores de la ECA/ARA II aumentan riesgo de hiperpotasemia.
Litio: aumento de niveles y toxicidad.
nursing_care: Evaluar PAS, frecuencia cardíaca y estado de hidratación antes de administrar.
Obtener electrolitos (Na, K, Cl) y creatinina basal.
Monitorear volumen urinario cada 2‑4 h; registrar peso diario.
Retener la dosis si PAS <90 mmHg, K⁺ <3.5 mEq/L o creatinina >2.0 mg/dL; notificar al médico.
patient_teaching: Tomar la dosis en la mañana para evitar nocturia.
Mantener una dieta rica en potasio (plátano, papas) salvo indicación contraria.
Reportar tinnitus, mareos o debilidad súbita.
Acudir a controles de laboratorio para electrolitos y función renal.

evidenced_by: aumento de peso >2 kg en 48 h
outcomes: Peso corporal estable: pérdida de ≤2 kg en 48 h.
Edema reducido o ausente en extremidades inferiores.

interventions.action: Registrar peso diario y comparar con peso basal.
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar cambios en el volumen de líquidos rápidamente.

interventions.action: Medir y registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Facilita el balance hídrico y la evaluación de la eficacia diurética.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de sobrecarga (edema, crepitantes) y de deshidratación (turgencia cutánea, mucosas secas).
interventions.rationale: Guía ajustes de la terapia y previene complicaciones.

interventions.action: Monitorear electrolitos y creatinina cada 24‑48 h.
interventions.rationale: Detecta desequilibrios y toxicidad renal inducidos por el diurético.

interventions.action: Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si PAS <90 mmHg o K⁺ <3.5 mEq/L.
interventions.rationale: Previene hipotensión grave y arritmias por hipopotasemia.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de la dieta baja en sodio (<2 g/día).
interventions.rationale: Reduce la retención de líquidos y mejora la respuesta al tratamiento.

en.summary: Furosemide is a loop diuretic used to eliminate excess fluid in heart failure and edema.
key_points: Blocks Na⁺/Cl⁻ in the loop of Henle, increasing diuresis.
Can cause hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and ototoxicity.
Monitor blood pressure, electrolytes, and renal function before and during treatment.
Avoid use with NSAIDs that reduce its efficacy.

mechanism: Inhibits reabsorption of sodium, chloride, and potassium in the loop of Henle.
Reduces the osmotic gradient, increasing water excretion.
Produces a potent and rapid diuresis.
indications: Pulmonary or peripheral edema due to renal or hepatic disease.
Refractory hypertension when combined with other antihypertensives.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to furosemide or other sulfonamides.
Anuria or acute renal failure without diuresis.
interactions: ACE inhibitors/ARBs increase risk of hyperkalemia.
nursing_care: Assess SBP, heart rate, and hydration status before administration.
Obtain baseline electrolytes (Na, K, Cl) and creatinine.
Monitor urine output every 2‑4 h; record daily weight.
Hold dose if SBP <90 mmHg, K⁺ <3.5 mEq/L, or creatinine >2.0 mg/dL; notify physician.
patient_teaching: Take the dose in the morning to avoid nocturia.
Maintain a potassium-rich diet (bananas, potatoes) unless contraindicated.
Report tinnitus, dizziness, or sudden weakness.
Attend lab checks for electrolytes and renal function.

outcomes: Stable body weight: loss ≤2 kg in 48 h.
Reduced or absent lower extremity edema.

interventions.action: Record daily weight and compare to baseline weight.
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of fluid volume changes.

interventions.action: Measure and record fluid intake and output every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates fluid balance and assessment of diuretic efficacy.

interventions.action: Assess signs of overload (edema, crackles) and dehydration (skin turgor, dry mucous membranes).
interventions.rationale: Guides therapy adjustments and prevents complications.

interventions.action: Monitor electrolytes and creatinine every 24‑48 h.
interventions.rationale: Detects imbalances and renal toxicity induced by the diuretic.

interventions.action: Hold dose and notify physician if SBP <90 mmHg or K⁺ <3.5 mEq/L.
interventions.rationale: Prevents severe hypotension and arrhythmias from hypokalemia.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of a low-sodium diet (<2 g/day).
interventions.rationale: Reduces fluid retention and improves treatment response.

key_points.0.quote: Loop diuretics block the reabsorption of sodium and chloride in the loop of Henle, which is located in the renal tubule.

key_points.1.quote: Adverse effects include severe anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reaction, excessive loss of water and electrolytes, ototoxicity, tinnitus and hearing loss, vertigo, dizziness, aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis,

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Due to the way the sodium pump works, loop diuretics also block the reabsorption of potassium.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Loop diuretics are a potent diuretic and could lead to diuresis with water and electrolyte depletion.

sections.indications.0.quote: 19.5.1 Identify the characteristics of the diuretic drugs used to treat heart failure.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Adverse Effects Severe anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reaction Orthostatic hypotension Excessive loss of wa

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Adverse effects include severe anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reaction, excessive loss of water and electrolytes, ototoxicity, tinnitus and hearing loss, vertigo, dizziness, aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis,

sections.interactions.1.quote: Typically, potassium-sparing diuretics, except for mineralocorticoid receptor agonists, are used sparingly in the treatment of heart failure because the combination of ACE inhibitor or ARB with a potassium-sparing diuretic can lead to increased potassium levels.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Take diuretic earlier in the day (morning) so that diuresis occurs before sleeping times.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Eat potassium-rich foods to replace potassium.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Report adverse effects such as dizziness or lightheadedness, fatigue, increased bleeding, tinnitus, weakness, and leg cramps to the provider.

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: (Doses exceeding 80 mg daily must be monitored carefully with frequent follow-up and laboratory monitoring.)
